parts.text:
4
The diagram shows two forces of 6.0 N acting on an object. The angle between the lines of action
of the two forces is 60°.
6.0 N
60°
6.0 N
What is the magnitude of the resultant force?
A
6.0 N
B
7.9 N
C
10 N
D
12 N

hints: Notice the diagram shows two equal $6.0\text{ N}$ arrows with $60^{\circ}$ between their lines of action, so they partly reinforce but do not line up fully.
Recall that the magnitude of the resultant of two vectors at angle $\theta$ follows $R^2 = F_1^2+F_2^2+2F_1F_2\cos\theta$.

Substitute $F_1 = F_2 = 6.0\text{ N}$ and $\theta = 60^{\circ}$ with $\cos 60^{\circ} = 0.5$, then take the square root and compare with the $6.0\text{ N}$, $7.9\text{ N}$, $10\text{ N}$ and $12\text{ N}$ options.
walkthrough: Identify the given vectors: two forces each $F = 6.0\text{ N}$ with angle $\theta = 60^{\circ}$ between them when placed tail to tail.
State the vector-addition rule: for two vectors the resultant magnitude satisfies $R^2 = F_1^2 + F_2^2 + 2F_1F_2\cos\theta$.
Set up the calculation with equal magnitudes: $R^2 = (6.0)^2 + (6.0)^2 + 2(6.0)(6.0)\cos 60^{\circ}$ in $\text{N}^2$.
Take the square root: $R = \sqrt{108}\text{ N} \approx 10.4\text{ N}$, which to the precision of the options is about $10\text{ N}$.
A value near $10\text{ N}$ is larger than one force but less than $12\text{ N}$ because the $60^{\circ}$ angle reduces the addition. This is option C.

A.explanation: This would be the size of one force alone and ignores the second $6.0\text{ N}$ force pulling partly in the same direction.

B.explanation: This value is too small for two equal $6.0\text{ N}$ forces only $60^{\circ}$ apart, where the components add strongly along the bisector.

C.explanation: Parallelogram addition gives $R = \sqrt{6.0^2+6.0^2+2\times 6.0\times 6.0\cos 60^{\circ}} \approx 10.4\text{ N}$, closest to $10\text{ N}$.

D.explanation: This is the arithmetic sum $6.0+6.0$, which only applies if the two forces were parallel at $0^{\circ}$, not $60^{\circ}$ apart.
